title: Networks: your addresses, who listens
summary: See your addresses, ask DNS, and what listening on 0.0.0.0 means.

text: Addresses, names and ports, on your machine.
- ip addr lists your own addresses (ifconfig on a Mac).
- dig asks DNS for a name's address.
- ping -c 3 sends 3 tries; without -c, ping runs until Ctrl-C.
- 203.0.113.10 is an example: dig shows you example.org's real addresses.
- 127.0.0.1 (localhost) is the machine itself: no other machine can connect.
- 0.0.0.0 means every address the machine has: open to the network.
- A database on 0.0.0.0 by mistake is a classic security hole.
- ss -tln: t = TCP, l = listening, n = numbers instead of names.
